text: What is true about tuples? (Select two answers.)

options.text: Tuples are immutable, which means that you're not allowed to change their contents.
The + operator can be applied to tuples and means concatenation.
All tuple elements must be of the same type.
The del keyword can be applied to a single tuple element in order to remove it.

explanation_en: Tuples are immutable – True: any attempt to change a tuple contents will raise the TypeError exception. The + operator – True: for example, (1,) + (2,) evaluates to (1, 2). All tuple elements must be of the same type – False: tuples of that kind would be very inflexible and of little use. The del keyword on a single element – False: immutable beings (including tuples) aren't able to mutate. You can use the del keyword to remove a tuple as a whole, but not to change its contents.

text: What is true about exceptions in Python? (Select two answers.)

options.text: An unhandled exception causes the program to terminate.
If any of the raised exceptions remains unhandled, an error message is printed, and program execution continues.
The code put inside the try branch may not be fully executed.
IndexError may be raised when you try to access a nonexistent dictionary element.

explanation_en: An unhandled exception causes the program to terminate – True. Handling exceptions is your task. If any of the raised exceptions remains unhandled, an error message is printed, and program execution continues – False. The error message which appears on screen announces the sad fact that the code is irrevocably terminated. The code put inside the try branch may not be fully executed – True. Such behavior makes the exceptions controllable. IndexError for a nonexistent dictionary element – False. This is a job for the KeyError exception.
